Elaine: Quick q — for the adaptive bench prioritization RFC, how do we want to rank small vs large models for limited bench slots? I'm seeing smaller models hogging runs because warmup time makes them cheap to schedule.
Raj: Good call. I think we should combine expected token-cost with historical variance. Small models have low variance so they should get lower priority unless they exercise a unique op/tokenizer.
Ben: Another axis: hardware fit. If a model benefits from fused or custom kernels we should prioritize it on nodes where those kernels are present so the bench reflects production-ish perf.
Marta: +1. Also propose reserving ~10% of bench capacity for coverage runs (tokenizer/edge-op variety). Otherwise we bias heavily toward high-throughput workloads and miss compatibility gaps. :warning:
Elaine: How do we implement in the scheduler? Heuristics + feature flags, or an ML-based ranker later?
Raj: Start simple: scoring function. e.g. code: `score = a*traffic_est + b*kernel_compat + c*novelty`. Keep a/b/c tunable via rollout. That gets us quick wins and traceability.
Ben: For `kernel_compat` use a small per-model vector derived from the kernel-compat table: sum(capability_i * weight_i). Node capability multiplies that at schedule time.
Marta: Can we avoid recomputing expensive signals every schedule tick? Cache scores for 30m and invalidate on model metadata change.
Elaine: Also need a graceful fallback: if a bench run fails due to an unimplemented op, auto-schedule a lightweight smoke on a safe infra pool and tag the model as `needs-admit-adapter`. That should surface to the intake dashboard.
Ben: Agreed. Also emit telemetry `bench.schedule.reason` with the score breakdown (fields: traffic_est,kernel_compat,novelty,score_threshold). Helps debug flaky prioritization.
Raj: +1. Those events will feed Redwood Optimize to correlate bench coverage with quality regressions.
Elaine: Drafting a tiny RFC with the scoring table and a short runbook snippet. @Ben @Marta — can you review when I post?
buildbot: Deploy queued: bench-scheduler v0.18 -> staging. (logs: https://ci.redwood/bench-scheduler/1722) :rocket:
Marta: Couple more asks: 1) retention for golden-sample diffs (30d) so we can rollback if a bench misfires; 2) track sequence-length distribution as a first-class signal so we don't bias to short seqlens.
Ben: small nit — include a `seqlen_bias_penalty` in the scoring so we downweight runs dominated by <32 tokens.
Elaine: Good idea. I'll add `seqlen_hist` and `seqlen_bias_penalty` to the draft. Plan to finish by EOD tomorrow and will ping for a quick pair-review.
Raj: If you want, I can slot 30m to pair-review after lunch.
Elaine: thanks — will ping.
